title: Intervention Threshold Sensitivity Analysis
description: Evaluates whether the predictive intervention conclusion is sensitive to the choice of entropy-drop threshold (5%–25%). The threshold defines the minimum relative drop in token entropy from generation 0 that triggers a switch from contaminated (α>0) to clean (α=0) training data.
threshold_definition: entropy_drop_pct = (entropy_gen0 - entropy_genT) / entropy_gen0 × 100. Intervention triggers when entropy_drop_pct exceeds threshold.

per_generation_trajectory.description: All thresholds 5%–25% produce identical trajectories since all trigger at gen 1

cross_alpha_sensitivity.description: Which contamination levels are detected at each threshold. Shows the only variation occurs at α=0.50 with threshold=25%.

0.00.note: Null (no contamination). Only threshold=5% produces false alarm.

0.10.note: Very low contamination. Undetectable at thresholds ≥10%.

0.50.note: Moderate contamination. Threshold=25% MISSES this level (22.4% < 25%). Only divergence among tested thresholds.

0.75.note: High contamination. All thresholds trigger at gen 1.

1.00.note: Full contamination. All thresholds trigger at gen 1.

delayed_intervention_comparison.description: Comparison of intervention at gen 1 vs gen 2 using actual experimental data (reactive_d1_s42 triggered at gen 2).

trigger_at_gen2_reactive.note: 1 generation delay causes 2.75x higher peak PPL but similar final convergence

robustness_summary.within_alpha_1_0: All 5 thresholds (5%–25%) produce IDENTICAL outcomes: trigger at gen 1, peak PPL 57.0, recovery in 1 generation, final PPL 21.3. The gen-1 entropy drop of 40.7% far exceeds even the most conservative threshold (25%).
robustness_summary.across_alpha_levels: Thresholds 10%–20% are functionally equivalent: they detect α≥0.50 at gen 1 with zero false alarms. Threshold 25% is slightly more conservative (misses α=0.50). Threshold 5% is overly sensitive (false alarm on null data).
robustness_summary.recommended_range: Any threshold in [10%, 22%] yields identical detection performance and zero false alarms. The reported 15% threshold is near the center of this safe operating range.
robustness_summary.sensitivity_verdict: NOT SENSITIVE. The intervention conclusion is robust to threshold choice across the entire 5%–25% range tested.

conclusion: The predictive intervention result is robust to threshold selection. All five tested thresholds (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%) trigger intervention at the same generation (gen 1) for α=1.0, producing identical recovery trajectories (peak PPL 57.0 → final PPL 21.3, 99.9% reduction vs. counterfactual collapse to PPL 15,024). The entropy signal at gen 1 (40.7% drop) exceeds even the most conservative threshold by a wide margin. Cross-α analysis shows thresholds 10%–20% form a robust operating band: zero false alarms on clean data (α=0.0 max drop = 7.5%) while detecting meaningful contamination (α≥0.50). The 15% threshold sits near the center of this safe range, confirming it is not a fragile post-hoc choice but falls within a broad plateau of equivalent performance.
